# Hugh Carrow

## Appearance

Hugh is an exceptionally handsome, high-statured youth with broad shoulders and a open, manly countenance. He has wavy chestnut hair and bright, direct light-brown or hazel eyes that often carry a mischievous expression. During a severe bout of illness, he appeared pale and thin.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P16](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0016), [v1 c15 P28](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0028), [v1 c28 P32](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0032), [v1 c37 P37](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0037), [v2 c19 P50](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0050), [v3 c39 P22](../source/v03-c39.md#nw-v03-c39-p0022)_

## Personality

Hugh is intelligent, studious, and ambitious, possessing individual perspectives and a resolve to make the most of life. He displays a lively appreciation for humor and enjoys teasing his peers, though he maintains high moral standards and guards his conduct vigilantly. Generous and considerate, he is willing to make sacrifices for others and shows dedicated leadership and tact among his classmates.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P16](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0016), [v1 c15 P28](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0028), [v1 c35 P3](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0003), [v1 c38 P38](../source/v01-c38.md#nw-v01-c38-p0038), [v2 c19 P51](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0051), [v3 c5 P0](../source/v03-c05.md#nw-v03-c05-p0000)_

## History

Hugh returned to Brierley after spending three years in Alberta with his ill father and a summer in New Brunswick. Re-entering school behind his age group, he quickly became Nell Harcourt's primary academic rival, eventually winning the graduation medal at Regent's Academy. When Nell sought a local teaching job to remain near home, Hugh generously relinquished his application for the Brierley school in her favor and took a position at Pale Sands instead to fund his future college tuition. He organized and served as president of the Brierley Village Improvement Society. Later, he attended Wexcombe College, where he was elected president of the Freshman Class, led the Freshmen to victory in the annual rush as football captain, and earned High Honors in Classics and the Cooper Prize upon graduation. Following a life-threatening bout of typhoid fever, he recovered and pursued medical studies. He eventually married Nell Harcourt and took over the medical practice of his great-uncle, Dr. David Carrow.
